newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: GREEK-TURKEY SQUABBLE OVERSHADOWS BUSINESS FORUM.
newsitem.headline: GREEK-TURKEY SQUABBLE OVERSHADOWS BUSINESS FORUM.

text.p: Greece has walked out of an international business forum in this Swiss mountain resort after condemning the participation of Turkish Cyprus as inadmissible.

In a statement late on Thursday, the Greek delegation expressed "great surprise" at the participation of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) in the annual forum, which brings together international business and political leaders.

Athens and Ankara have been at loggerheads over Cyprus since its virtual partition in 1974 when Turkish troops took over the north of the island after a coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruling Greece.
"The Greek delegation condemns this inadmissible behaviour by the forum and refuses to participate," the Greek statement said at the start of the four-day forum.
It said that northern Cyprus, recognised only by Turkey, did not exist as an entity in terms of international law.

The founder of the Crans Montana Forum, Jean-Paul Carteron, said he felt "great sadness" at the incident in a statement. But he said the gathering was not a diplomatic event but "an occasion for those of good faith to cooperate towards building peace through concrete business contacts."
Greece was due to be represented at the forum by its Secretary of State for Economic Affairs, Alexandros Baltas.
